title: The Glad look on his face
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：glad　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 glad 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the warden wrote of ① a glad look on his face in the register, and everybody in the centre said at once that it was ② gladder than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the warden, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the glad ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the gladdest look on his face anybody in the centre had ever seen, or so the register for June 1976 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too glad to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the resident who had come to help; the glad ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the notice at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a glad helper in the kitchen, and said that no resident in his right mind would call it ⑥ as glad as the helper in the kitchen they had once had in the old centre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was glad or not, and he said so.

By 1989 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the register. What the line asked for was ⑦ something glad, and nothing besides. The resident from the next centre called the whole plan ⑧ quite glad; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the register kept the names of the glad ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1992, twice over, she wrote of another glad look on his face in the same register, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ gladder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The gladdest helper in the kitchen in the whole centre, she said in 1994, was the one she could never quite name; the glad ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 高兴（前置定语 a glad look on his face：1982 年管理员在登记册里记下的那件高兴的喜色）
B. adj. 高兴／乐意（比较级 gladder than：文中两处，一处比他脸上的喜色，一处比预想）
C. adj. 高兴／乐意（最高级 the gladdest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 高兴（表语 too glad to do：母亲觉得它太高兴，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 乐意（前置定语 a glad helper in the kitchen：叔叔把整件事称作一桩乐意的人）
F. adj. 乐意（同级比较 as glad as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩厨房里乐意帮忙的人相比）
G. adj. 乐意（后置定语 something glad：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 乐意（受程度副词修饰 quite glad：那位居民的评价）

items.q: a glad look on his face
the gladdest look on his face anybody
a glad helper in the kitchen
The gladdest helper in the kitchen in

answers.why: glad 意为“高兴”，1982 年管理员在登记册里记下的是“一件高兴的喜色”，此处作前置定语 a glad look on his face。
glad 意为“高兴”，此处用比较级 gladder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
glad 意为“高兴”，登记册上 六月 那行字说它是社区中心里最高兴的一件，故用最高级 the gladdest look on his face。
glad 意为“高兴”，母亲认为这件东西“太高兴了，谁也用不上”，too glad to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
glad 意为“乐意”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩乐意的人”，此处作前置定语 a glad helper in the kitchen。
glad 意为“乐意”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩厨房里乐意帮忙的人一样乐意”，同级比较用 as glad as。
glad 意为“乐意”，登记册上那半行字要的是“乐意的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something glad。
glad 意为“乐意”，邻社区中心来的那位居民认为这套计划“相当乐意”，quite 修饰原级 glad。
glad 意为“乐意”，1992 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要乐意”，故用比较级 gladder than。
glad 意为“乐意”，母亲 1994 年说的是“整个社区中心里最乐意的那一桩”，故用最高级 the gladdest helper in the kitchen。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1982 年，管理员在登记册里记下了一件高兴的喜色。（a glad look on his face）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更高兴。（gladder than …）
母亲觉得它太高兴，谁也用不上。（too glad to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩乐意的人。（a glad helper in the kitchen）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩厨房里乐意帮忙的人一样乐意。（as glad as …）
到了 1989 年，登记册上只剩半行字：要的是一件乐意的东西。（something glad）
answers: In 1982 the warden wrote of a glad look on his face in the register.
Everybody said it was gladder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too glad to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a glad helper in the kitchen.
He said nobody would call it as glad as the helper in the kitchen they had once had.
By 1989 the register asked for nothing but something glad.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 glad 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1982 the warden wrote of a glad look on his face in the register, and nobody forgot it.
It was the gladdest look on his face in the centre, or so the register says.
My mother thought it too glad to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a glad helper in the kitchen, and nobody argued with him.
The resident from the next centre called the plan quite glad, and everybody laughed.
The glad ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
